text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Greek press speculates that the U.N. will propose the name "Skopje" as a compromise that could be acceptable to both countries in their dispute over what to call the former Yugoslav republic of Macedonia.
- Customs-free regime between Yugoslavia and Macedonia enters into force today.
- Over 60 million kilos of grapes picked in the Tikves region vinyards over the weekend. More than 20 thousand people participated in the grape picking.

- Macedonia will support the speedy reintegration of Yugoslavia into international organisations, but not as the sole successor of the former Yugoslavia, said foreign minister Ljubomir Frckovski Saturday on his return from New York.
- Macedonia signed a declaration on strengthening friendly relations with Bulgaria, Ljubomir Frckovski said.

- Radio Tirana comments that the main reason for extending the U.N. Protection Force's (UNPREDEP) mandate in Macedonia is the Albanian-language Tetovo university. The Macedonian government's refusal to recognise the institution generates inter-ethnic tensions.
- Administration of Tetovo university confirms that the institution accepted 27,000 German marks from the ethnic Albanian PDP party which is a member of the governing coalition.
- Macedonian defence minsiter Blagoje Handziski is visiting Belgrade today.
- Greece's first major investment in Macedonia to be in the Strumica tobacco industry and in two mines. The total Macedonian-Greek trade by the end of the year to be $100 million.
